blocker_evidence.C2_GRADIENT_SEVERING_CONDITION_UNRESOLVE: Two specified reconstructions fail to reproduce the defective endpoint. v1 (seeded random init) and v2 (authenticated u0 bytes, sha256 19fb0c25 verified, historical geometry views=4 mask_fraction=0.4 target_blocks=16 batch=128 microbatch=8 64 backwards fp16 AMP GradScaler checkpointing) both give 0 of 48 dead mandatory tensors, with Q/K/V gradient norms of order 1e1 to 4.6e4, far above fp16 subnormal. The frozen bisection therefore never started and the fp32-loss-operand hypothesis was never reached: neither confirmed nor refuted. Separately, the saved checkpoint online_gradients are a capture-timing artifact: the trainer zeroes gradients immediately before capture, and u0205 holds 0 of 108 nonzero, not 48. The surviving evidence is the AdamW moment state, which zero_grad does not touch: 48 of 123 entries hold both moments exactly zero after 205 updates. That remains unexplained. Largest untested difference is the input distribution; a new prospective contract is required.

blocker_evidence.SEALED_HOLDOUT_MEMBERSHIP_PUBLICLY_READA: results/v4/stage81a2_split_registry.csv on public main discloses which donors are in the sealed_holdout split, together with the freeze seed and assignment method. NOT a privacy or PII issue: the owner confirms all donor data was obtained from already-public databases (SEA-AD is published by the Allen Institute), so donor identifiers and pathology are already in the public domain and require no remediation. The remaining issue is narrower and purely one of split concealment: a sealed holdout assumes membership is unknown until the evaluation contract is frozen, so a publicly readable membership list makes a future sealed-evaluation claim contestable regardless of whether anyone looked. Nothing to repair in git; if a sealed-holdout evaluation is proposed later, re-seal with a fresh seed and partition instead.
